checkedFactsAndBoundaries: The 2001 Freak introduced silicon escape wheels in a production mechanical wristwatch, not an entirely silicon mechanism or the first silicon hairspring.
The upper gear-train/regulator carrier turns once per hour. The lower barrel-associated hour indication turns over twelve hours. Not every component of the calibre rotates hourly.
The original watch uses back-bezel winding and upper-bezel setting. The current Freak X has a crown, so crownless cannot describe every Freak.

Carrousel is the manufacturer's term for the orbital architecture. A one-hour indicating carrier is not conflated with a conventional one-minute Breguet tourbillon. The original is not indiscriminately described as flying.

Forestier-Kasapi supplied the rotating-movement concept, Schnyder backed the project, Oechslin reworked the architecture and developed the Dual Direct, and Gygax proposed silicon for the wheels. No invented workshop dialogue or precise scene is supplied.

The two original impulse wheels mesh and counterrotate. They alternately impulse a roller on the balance arbor directly. A separate rocking member locks each wheel in turn, stopping both through their mesh.
US6301981B1 is the primary source for phase order and the illustrative 25 teeth including five long teeth. Its 4 Hz numerical example is not a measurement of the first production Freak.
The subsequent Dual Ulysse introduces an intervening impulse part. Two wheels or DIAMonSIL treatment alone do not identify an unchanged 2001 Dual Direct escapement.
No universal zero-friction, wholly maintenance-free or microsecond tooth-contact accuracy claim is made.

016-88/P001 belongs to the circa-2001 pink-gold prototype documented by Phillips. 026-88/UN-01 identifies the later example catalogued by Christie's. The manufacturer's archive cutout is not assigned an unverified unique specimen code.

UN-240, 3 Hz, 21,600 vph, 90 hours and 229 parts are current Freak ONE data. UN-230, 72 hours and 214 parts follow the current blue Freak X manufacturer page. Historical reviews with other component counts are not silently substituted.
